name: NVIC Priority Planner
blurb: interrupt priorities in order, with preemption conflicts
intro: Sorts your interrupts the way the Cortex-M NVIC does (group priority, then subpriority), encodes the priority bytes and PRIGROUP, and runs a worst-case response-time analysis: each handler's own time, the time it is blocked by its own group, and the time handlers above it preempt it, against its deadline. It flags shared levels, deadline-order inversions and RTOS-API calls above the FreeRTOS syscall limit.

inputs.label: Preemption bits (priority grouping)
inputs.help: STM32 HAL NVIC_PRIORITYGROUP_n uses n preemption bits.

inputs.label: Interrupts
inputs.help: Priority 0 is the most urgent. Times in µs; deadline blank = period.

usage: Give the implemented priority bits (2, 3, 4 or 8), the preemption bits ('all' or 0-7), an optional FreeRTOS syscall limit, and a table of interrupts with name, priority, subpriority, handler time, period and optional deadline in µs, and whether it calls the RTOS API (yes/no). It returns the interrupts in NVIC order with IPR byte values, blocking, preemption and worst-case response times against deadlines, the CPU load, a conflicts table, HAL code, and result.irqs for the drawing. Use it to choose priorities before writing NVIC setup or to explain a missed interrupt.
sources: Arm Armv7-M Architecture Reference Manual B1.5.4 (priority grouping) and B3.2.6 AIRCR.PRIGROUP
Joseph & Pandya, 'Finding response times in a real-time system', Computer Journal 1986; Audsley et al. 1993 (blocking term)
FreeRTOS 'Running the RTOS on an ARM Cortex-M core' (configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY)
